Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

saved = rlm.harness.create_memory(title="ARC: compress repeated row/column bands", content="When an ARC grid has a regular background crossed by full-length colored horizontal/vertical stripes (sometimes with interrupted/overwritten intersections), inspect one demo for a compression rule. Output may keep every stripe row/column and collapse each uniform background gap to one cell/row/column. For k horizontal stripes and m vertical stripes this often yields dimensions (2k+1) x (2m+1): alternating one representative background band and each original stripe. Preserve stripe ordering/colors and sample the actual stripe crossings; do not assume all intersections preserve the vertical stripe or horizontal stripe uniformly, because input may encode selective overwrites. In the solved example, 10x11 with horizontal lines rows 1,6 and vertical cols 3,8 compressed to 5x5, keeping line positions at output rows/cols 1 and 3. For a 12x13 test with horizontal rows 3,6,9 and vertical cols 2,5,7,10, compression produced 7x9. Choose any representative from uniform gap bands, then verify values from line rows/columns, especially crossings.", path="arc", global_=True)
print(saved)
